Question B-007-005-007.

Why the correct answer is right: High sunspot numbers can raise usable frequencies so upper HF and sometimes even slightly higher frequencies support long-distance paths.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "High frequency radio signals are absorbed": High frequency radio signals are absorbed describes a disturbance or lower-region loss, not the usual high-sunspot improvement in upper-HF propagation.
- sourceIndex 2: "Frequencies up to 100 MHz or higher are normally usable for long-distance communication": Frequencies up to 100 MHz or higher are normally usable for long-distance communication overstates the usual effect; that range is not normally available by ionospheric propagation.
- sourceIndex 3: "High frequency radio signals become weak and distorted": High frequency radio signals become weak and distorted is not the general high-sunspot trend; many higher HF paths improve.
